HEART FAILURE
Normally the heart pumps adequate blood to perfuse tissues 
and meet metabolic needs (see Figure 33-10). In heart failure 
(HF), formerly called congestive heart failure, the heart can-
not provide adequate blood flow to the rest of the body, caus-
ing symptoms of fatigue, shortness of breath (dyspnea), and 
fluid retention. Diseases of the heart (valves, muscle, blood

vessels) and vasculature can lead to HF (see Pathophysiology 
and Care Management Algorithm: Heart Failure). HF can be 
right-sided or left-sided or can affect both sides of the heart. 
It is further categorized as systolic failure when the heart 
cannot pump, or eject, blood efficiently out of the heart or 
diastolic failure, meaning the heart cannot fill with blood as 
it should.
